result.summary: The main finding is measured, not theoretical: in the trader cloud session the news engine died three times today (2026-11-10), each time 236-296 seconds after the turn that started it ended (it lived 5.0-5.5 minutes), because a cloud VM "pauses after a few minutes without activity" (Claude docs) and a paused VM keeps its files but not its processes; nohup and setsid did not help. From the 14:30 UTC open to 15:11:54 UTC the engine was up 21.8 of 41.9 minutes (52.0%). While it was down from 14:18:50 to 14:38:38 UTC, MU traded through its stop of 708.97 (one-minute lows 707.92, 702.36, 703.69 and 708.75 between 14:31 and 14:35 UTC; the 14:32 bar closed at 704.35) and was not sold, so the owner's "sell at -3%, no exceptions" rule was skipped by an outage; a sale near 704.35 would have lost about $160, and only by luck MU is back above the 730.90 entry (732-738 at 15:13-15:21 UTC). One thing kept the VM awake: the engine relaunched at 14:54:00 UTC as a harness-tracked background command was still alive at 15:38:10 UTC (44 minutes, across idle gaps of 13.0 and 25.5 minutes; one launch only), but the documented cap is 2 hours per command, so it should be stopped near 16:54 UTC unless the limit is raised with the BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable. A restart "within one second" is real for a process on a machine that is itself alive: in a scratch drill a kill -9 was followed by the replacement's first heartbeat in 337-449 ms (median 404 ms, n=6), a hang was caught 2.18 s after heartbeats stopped (2 s threshold), and a crash loop was stopped after 6 starts. A restarted engine could check a stop 0.73 s after process start if stops were checked first; as coded it polls 74 feeds and scores first, at least 2.33 s plus scoring. What cannot be done in a second is bringing back a paused or reclaimed VM: each scheduled task runs at most hourly, the two watchdogs are 30 minutes apart, firing was 37-393 s late (n=7) and a turn took 25-144 s, so the worst case is about 39 minutes, and it is unbounded if the trader session is stuck or the weekly model limit is hit (the trader session already shows "allowed_warning" on its 7-day window, reset 2026-11-15 06:00 UTC). The supervisor should be four layers: an engine that can be supervised (stop check first, exit codes, one-instance lock), a tiny Python parent that restarts with back-off and a crash-loop limit and writes an uptime log, health checks with heartbeats for feeds, quotes, scorer, chains and slots, and outside checks. The outside checks are a dead-man's switch on ntfy (a scheduled message pushed back at every heartbeat, delivered by ntfy when pings stop; free tier 250 messages a day) and a second watcher session. Every unattended job must live outside the main chat: since it became limited to the owner's trusted devices a self-reminder there failed with ACCESS_DENIED, and all 8 enabled trader tasks are already bound to other sessions. An LLM turn must not be the process supervisor: each watchdog wake of the trader session costs $0.24-$0.80 of usage at list prices (343k-token context), and that session runs claude-opus-5-5 although the standing order is Fable 5.2. Hosting, in order: fix the cloud setup first ($0); the owner's PC is free but the engine does not import on Windows as written (fcntl) and nothing runs after a reboot until he signs in; a VPS at $4.00-€5.49 a month is the only host built to be always on but needs his account, payment and Claude token; GitHub Actions is wrong for the live engine (5-minute cron, runs delayed or dropped, 6-hour job cap, and the repository is a public fork). The alert "last run SUCCEEDED" on a scheduled task means only that the wake was delivered (finished 10-20 ms after firing), so today nothing detects a slot that fired and failed.

options.name: Failure map: 15 parts that can stop, with detection, speed and restart or containment (the supervisor's checklist)
options.what_it_gives: 1) Engine process dies (crash, kill, out of memory). Detect: the parent's wait on the child, under 0.1 s. Restart: 0.34-0.45 s. Today: an LLM watchdog, up to about 39 min. 2) Engine hangs or a step runs long (one scorer call may block 90 s per batch of 12, and stops are checked last in step()). Detect: heartbeat older than a threshold (120 s). Restart: SIGTERM, 5 s, SIGKILL, new child. Contain: stop loop on its own timer, off the scorer path. 3) Cloud VM pauses when idle or is reclaimed (the cause of today's 3 deaths). The in-VM supervisor dies with it. Detect: only from outside, by the dead-man alert (6-9 min) or the next watchdog task. Prevent: run the supervisor as a harness-tracked background command. Restart: next scheduled turn. A pause keeps files; a reclaim keeps only what was pushed to git. 4) Background-command time limit in cloud sessions (30 min default, 2 h maximum): the harness stops the engine and wakes the session. Today's engine should be stopped near 16:54 UTC. Fix: raise BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, or relaunch on the stop notice. 5) Headline feed slow or dead (Yahoo RSS): a failed fetch returns an empty list silently, which looks like 'no news'. Detect each poll (20 s): feeds answering out of 74, age of the newest headline, latency_s; alert after 3 bad polls. Contain: no buys happen; stops are unaffected. 6) Stale or missing quote: already there (buys blocked on a quote older than 3 min; urgent alert after 300 s blind on a held name). Gap: no second quote source, so the stop cannot act while blind. 7) Scorer CLI (claude -p) fails, times out or hits the usage limit: today it returns nothing and prints one line; the headlines are marked seen and lost (147 on 2026-11-09). Detect: journal every failure with its reason; alert after 3 failed batches. Contain: stops-only mode keeps running; retry while the headline is still fresh. 8) Scheduled slot late, missing or failed. Detect: one receipt line per slot (state/slots.jsonl) checked against expected times by the watcher. Restart: fire the task again (30 fires an hour per task); the cycle is idempotent. 9) Trader session blocked (permission prompt, long desk turn, compaction at 784k tokens; 343k used now): later scheduled messages wait behind it. Detect: stale receipts and heartbeat seen from the watcher session. Contain: push to the owner; the in-VM supervisor keeps the engine alive meanwhile. 10) Broken hash chain: found every 300 s by the engine and at every cycle; fail-closed halt and urgent alert exist. The supervisor must NOT restart it, but ChainBroken exits with code 0, the same as end of day, so it needs its own exit code. Stops are not checked while halted. Prevention: one writer per chained file; journal.append has no lock, so two engines would fork the chain; a file lock must replace today's pgrep check. 11) Git push conflicts between sessions. Detect: non-zero exit. Contain: one save script (commit own files, pull --rebase, push, 5 tries, under a lock), one writer per file family, run every 5 min so a reclaim loses at most 5 min of state (today up to 30). 12) Engine running old code after a pull. Detect: the heartbeat carries the git revision the engine started with. Restart: controlled restart between steps. 13) Dashboard (hourly LLM slot). Detect: the page compares its own 'updated at' stamp with the clock and turns red after 90 min in market hours; slot receipt. Restart: re-fire the slot. 14) Alert channel: a failed ntfy post is not retried (except the blind-stop alert); crypto alerts wait in quiet hours 23:00-08:00 Israel by the owner's choice. Detect: the dead-man covers 'the engine cannot speak'; failed sends go to an outbox and are retried; second path is the Claude app push from LLM turns. 15) Model usage limit: every scheduled turn and the scorer stop together. Detect: scorer errors, missing receipts, the session record. Contain: only code that needs no model turn keeps running (stops, supervisor). It cannot be restarted before the limit resets.

Measured: 74 of 74 feeds answered, one full poll 1.60 s, newest headline 109 s old, one quote 0.40 s (read-only timing script, 15:17 UTC). Measured: at 14:13:13 UTC 'git pull --rebase' refused on a dirty tree with git's own hint 'Please commit or stash them' (stash is banned). Measured: the 15:38 UTC pull changed news_live.py while the engine started at 14:54 kept running the earlier code. Measured: scheduled-task last_run shows fired_at and finished_at 10-20 ms apart with status SUCCEEDED (list_triggers), and the tool text says it records only that the wake was delivered. Measured: trader session rate_limit_info = seven_day, allowed_warning, resetsAt 1794722400 (2026-11-15 06:00 UTC); context 343k of 1M tokens, auto-compact at 784k. options.effort: About half a day to turn the list into checks and tests; the items that touch risk rules go through the rule-4 gate.
options.risks: A check that has never caught a fault in a drill is not trusted (basic law 2, item 5). The list is as complete as one day of evidence allows; the cause of the 2026-11-09 17:26 UTC death was not verified (it is consistent with an idle pause).

options.name: Layer 0: make the engine supervisable (stop check first, exit codes, one-instance lock, journaled failures, blind-window stop replay)
options.what_it_gives: The stop check runs first in every step and on its own timer, so a slow scorer or feed cannot blind it, and after any restart it runs before anything else. Distinct exit codes: 0 = end of day, 3 = fail-closed halt (broken chain, never restarted), anything else = crash (restarted). A file lock held for the life of the process makes a second engine impossible. The heartbeat carries pid, phase, step time and the git revision. Scorer failures, dropped headlines and feed health are journaled instead of printed. Blind-window replay: on start, if a name is held and the last heartbeat is old, read the one-minute bars since then; if the low crossed the stop, sell at the current live quote and report it.
options.measured_or_documented: Measured (read-only timing in this container, 2026-11-10 15:17 UTC): import 0.32 s, book load 0.00 s, chain check of the 4 news journals 0.01 s, one poll of 74 feeds 1.60 s, one MU quote 0.40 s; so 0.73 s from process start to a stop check if stops go first, against at least 2.33 s plus scoring as coded. Measured: MU one-minute lows of 707.92, 702.36, 703.69 and 708.75 at 14:31-14:35 UTC against the stop 708.9732 while the engine was down 14:18:50-14:38:38 UTC; no sale (Yahoo chart MU 1d/1m, fetched 15:13:46 and 15:21:52 UTC).
options.effort: 1-2 days with tests and the rule-4 gate (time machine does not apply to the news rule; quant-critic and unit tests do).
options.owner_must_do: Decide one rule: after an outage, if the price crossed the stop while the engine was blind, should it sell at the next live quote? (It only reduces risk.) Decide also whether a broken journal chain may still sell held names.
options.risks: A replay sale fills below the stop when the price gapped (that is what a stop costs). Yahoo one-minute bars can be late or missing. These changes touch risk code, so they need the gate before they land.

options.name: Layer 1: in-VM process supervisor (a tiny Python parent, launched as a harness-tracked background command)
options.what_it_gives: About 100 lines of standard-library Python. It starts the engine as its child and restarts it at once if it had run 60 s or more, otherwise with back-off 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60 s. Crash-loop limit: 5 restarts in 10 minutes, then it stops, sends an urgent alert and exits with code 75 (which wakes the session). Hang: heartbeat older than 120 s, then SIGTERM, 5 s, SIGKILL. It honours the exit codes of layer 0, writes state/uptime.jsonl (start, exit, hang, restart, tripped, and a mark every 60 s so a VM pause shows as a gap), runs the state save script every 5 minutes, and on every restart tells the owner what stopped, from when to when, and which positions were unprotected with the low against the stop in that window. A Python parent rather than a shell loop because back-off, crash-loop limit, hang detection and the JSON log live in one file that also runs on a PC or a VPS (on a VPS systemd replaces it).
options.measured_or_documented: Measured (scratch drill with a dummy child that imports pandas and requests, 2026-11-10 15:16 UTC): kill -9 to first heartbeat of the replacement 337-449 ms, median 404 ms, n=6; hang detected 2.18 s after heartbeats stopped at a 2 s threshold, new child 0.01 s later; crash loop: 6 starts, back-offs 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 s, tripped with exit 75 after 20.5 s; exit code 3 was not restarted. Measured: nohup (twice) and setsid nohup with disown (once) did not survive; the engine launched at 14:54:00 UTC with run_in_background and timeout 7,200,000 ms was alive at 15:11:56 and 15:38:10 UTC (pid 664, heartbeat 15:38:01), and the session worker stayed up between turns (780,740 ms and 1,529,783 ms idle). Documented: cloud background commands get 30 minutes or up to 2 hours; 'Set BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS above 7200000 to raise the 2-hour maximum'.
options.cost: $0 cash. Usage falls: today's 16 watchdog wakes a day cost $0.24-$0.80 each at list prices and most become unnecessary.
options.effort: 1 day including the drill on a copy of the state.
options.owner_must_do: Approve one environment variable on an approval card (BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, for example 32400000 = 9 hours).
options.risks: Keep-awake rests on one launch observed for 44 minutes; the feature is a research preview and may change. The supervisor dies with the VM, so it never replaces the outside layer. It becomes a single point of failure, so it must stay tiny, tested and drilled. The prototype is a research file and has not passed the gate.

options.name: Layer 3a: dead-man's switch on ntfy (an alert when the pings STOP)
options.what_it_gives: The supervisor re-publishes one scheduled message with a fixed id every 3 minutes with a 6-minute delay. While pings arrive nothing is shown. When they stop, ntfy.sh itself delivers 'news engine silent for 6+ minutes, stops are not being checked' to the owner's phone. At the end of the day the supervisor cancels it. It still works when the thing that died is the VM, the trader session, the scheduler or the model limit. One more ping per daily job (quant open and close, crypto decide and fill) with a longer delay.
options.measured_or_documented: Documented (docs.ntfy.sh/publish, seen 2026-11-10): the docs carry this exact pattern as a 'dead man's switch' example (curl -H 'In: 5m' ... ntfy.sh/mytopic/heartbeat-check); 'the minimum delay you can set is 10 seconds and the maximum delay is 3 days'; a scheduled message is replaced by publishing with the same sequence id and cancelled with DELETE /topic/sequence_id; 'On ntfy.sh, the daily message limit is 250'; messages cached 12 hours. The ntfy status page listed no incidents from Oct 27 to Nov 10, 2026 and shows no uptime figure. Not drilled by me: this research was not allowed to publish anything.
options.cost: $0. A 3-minute cadence over a 7.5-hour day is 150 pings, under 250. If the limit is hit: $5 a month (2,500 a day).
options.effort: 2-3 hours plus a drill (stop the pings on purpose and time the alert).
options.owner_must_do: nothing (the ntfy app and topic already exist; AITRADER_NTFY_TOPIC is set in the environment). Pay $5 a month only if the free limit turns out too small.
options.risks: Detection is 6-9 minutes, not seconds, and it tells him without restarting anything. Unverified: whether replaced messages count against the 250 a day, and whether the limit is shared with other users behind the cloud proxy's address (a 429 would silence alerts). The topic name works like a password and the repository is a public fork, so it must never be committed.

options.name: Layer 3b: watcher in a second cloud session, plus slot receipts
options.what_it_gives: A separate session with two hourly tasks at minutes 22 and 52, so that together with the trader's 07 and 37 something checks every 15 minutes. Each run reads the heartbeat signal the supervisor publishes outward and the slot receipts on the branch; if either is stale it fires the trader's watchdog task at once and pushes one Hebrew line to the owner. It must not be the main chat (scheduled tasks can no longer wake it) and not the trader session (it cannot watch itself). Standing rule: never attach the owner's computer to the trader or watcher session, because that limits a session to his trusted devices for good.
options.measured_or_documented: Documented: 'Expressions that run more often than once per hour are rejected'; 100 scheduled runs an hour per account; 30 manual or API fires an hour per task; runs on the hour 'can start several minutes late' (Claude scheduled-tasks docs, seen 2026-11-10). Measured firing delay today: 393, 355, 39, 66, 37, 285, 39 s (n=7); the minute-07 task was 285-393 s late three times out of three. Measured: all 8 enabled trader tasks are bound to the trader session or the crypto session, none to the main chat (list_triggers 15:07 UTC); the day-one audit log records a self-reminder to the main chat failing with ACCESS_DENIED. From the 2026-11-09 build log: fresh sessions per run could not push (403), so the watcher only reads, fires and notifies. Unverified: whether a child session gets the tools to read another session's status.
options.cost: $0 cash. Usage per run not measured (the trader session's wakes cost $0.24-$0.80 because of its 343k-token context; a small watcher should cost less).
options.owner_must_do: nothing beyond approving the creation prompts if they appear.
options.risks: It shares the same account limit and the same platform as the thing it watches, so it is not independent of a platform outage or the usage limit; only the ntfy dead-man is. It adds LLM wakes. Scheduled tasks are a research preview.

options.name: Uptime log, dashboard row and fault drills
options.what_it_gives: uptime.jsonl gives a daily uptime percentage of session minutes and a list of gaps with the positions that were unprotected. The dashboard gets one row: uptime today, age of the last heartbeat, restarts, feeds answering, scorer failures, age of the data. A weekly drill, with no open position or on a copy: kill the engine, freeze the heartbeat, feed a stale quote, break a chain on a copy, block the alert channel, skip a slot. Each detector must fire and the result is logged.
options.measured_or_documented: Measured, and the first entry of the log: down 13:19:18-14:13:22 UTC (54.1 min, before the open), 14:18:50-14:38:38 (19.8 min, across the open, MU stop crossed and not sold), 14:43:41-14:55:09 (11.5 min); uptime 52.0% of the first 41.9 session minutes. On 2026-11-09 the equity log shows one gap of 959 s (17:23:00-17:38:59 UTC) against a median spacing of 309 s (state/news_equity.jsonl).
options.effort: Half a day, then about 30 minutes a week for the drill.
options.risks: None material. Without the drills the other layers are untested promises.

options.name: Hosting 1: stay in Claude cloud sessions, with layers 0 to 3
options.what_it_gives: No new account; the scorer and the LLM slots already live here. Restart delay: a crashed process under 1 s; an idle pause is prevented while the tracked command runs; a VM lost anyway waits for the next scheduled turn, worst case 30 min spacing + 393 s firing delay + 144 s turn = about 39 min (about 24 min with four staggered tasks); a model limit or a blocked session has no bound. What survives: files on a pause, only pushed git state on a reclaim, the conversation always.
options.measured_or_documented: Documented: 'after a few minutes without activity, a session's VM pauses with its files saved, and a paused VM can later be reclaimed'; background work is not restored after a reclaim; 4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM, 30 GB disk; 'no separate charge for the cloud VM' (Claude docs, seen 2026-11-10). Measured in this VM: 4 CPUs, 16,086 MB. Measured: turns of the trader session took 25-144 s and cost $0.24-$0.80 at list prices ($2.23 for the first cold one); session total $11.81 from 2026-11-09 10:58 UTC to 2026-11-10 15:38 UTC. The four documentation pages the task named (session.resources, environment.setup_script, environment.dependencies, remote_control.setup) hold handling instructions only and no lifetime numbers.
options.cost: $0 a month in cash; it draws on the subscription's weekly limit.
options.effort: Included in layers 0 to 3 (about 3-4 days in total).
options.owner_must_do: Approve the environment variable. Switch the trader session to the model he ordered (it runs claude-opus-5-5; his standing order is Fable 5.2) with /model in that session.
options.risks: Research preview, no uptime promise. Everything sits on one account's weekly limit (trader session at 'allowed_warning', reset 2026-11-15 06:00 UTC). Keep-awake seen on one launch only. One session carries news, quant, crypto and dashboard, so one stuck turn delays all four.

options.name: Hosting 2: the owner's Windows PC (engine and supervisor as a native local process, a local Claude session for the LLM parts)
options.what_it_gives: No idle pause and no background time limit, on a machine that already runs four Claude sessions around the clock under a 60-second watchdog. Restart delay: a crash under 1 s with the same supervisor (Windows Task Scheduler alone restarts no faster than every 1 minute); after a Windows reboot nothing runs until he signs in, which has no bound. What survives: everything on disk.
options.measured_or_documented: Code fact: aitrader/news_live.py line 16 imports fcntl, and Python documents fcntl as 'Availability: Unix, not WASI', so the engine does not start on native Windows as written. Documented: ZoneInfo needs the tzdata package where the system has no time-zone database, 'notably Windows'; requirements.txt does not list it. Measured: engine import peaks at 73 MB of memory. Documented: 'A local session ... has no time limit on background commands'; Remote Control server mode exits after roughly 10 minutes without network; Task Scheduler restart interval 'minimum time allowed is 1 minute'. From the other project's rules: 15.6 GB RAM, at most one heavy app, watchdog restarts after 2 misses with at most 4 restarts an hour, and 'after a Windows reboot nothing runs until someone signs in'.
options.effort: 1-2 days: port the file lock, add tzdata, a launcher and a watchdog entry, a state push path, a drill.
options.owner_must_do: Agree to run it on his PC, keep the PC on, and sign in to Windows after every reboot.
options.risks: The reboot gap is unbounded and he is mostly away from the PC. Home power and internet. Memory shared with Unity and Blender; the data disk is USB. Two projects on one machine. It must be a native local process: a cloud session attached to the PC becomes device-bound and cannot be woken by scheduled tasks.

options.name: Hosting 3: a small always-on VPS with systemd
options.what_it_gives: The only option built to be always on: systemd restarts the engine after a crash and at boot with nobody signed in, can kill a hung service, and there is no idle pause or 2-hour cap. Restart delay: about 1 s for a crash; a host reboot about 1-2 minutes (not measured). What survives: the disk.
options.measured_or_documented: Documented: systemd RestartSec 'Defaults to 100ms', Restart=always, WatchdogSec puts a silent service in a failed state. Prices seen 2026-11-10: Hetzner CPX02 (1 vCPU, 1 GB, 20 GB) €5.49 a month excluding VAT, with the page showing 'currently unavailable' on its create buttons; DigitalOcean $4.00 a month (1 vCPU, 512 MiB) and $6.00 (1 GiB). Documented: 'claude setup-token' gives a one-year token tied to the subscription for scripts. Provider uptime: unverified.
options.effort: 1 day to set up, then patching.
options.owner_must_do: Open the account and pay himself. Generate the Claude token himself and put it on the server (never in chat).
options.risks: A server to patch and secure, with a long-lived token on someone else's machine. Scoring still draws on the same weekly limit. More than a paper book that needs about 7.5 hours a day requires today.

options.name: Hosting 4: GitHub Actions cron
options.what_it_gives: Not a host for the live engine. It could later carry the deterministic daily jobs (quant open and close, crypto decide and fill: plain Python that tolerates delay), which would free them from the model limit, as the 2026-11-09 research already proposed. That depends on moving ai-trader to its own private repository (backlog item 14).
options.measured_or_documented: Documented (GitHub docs, seen 2026-11-10): 'The shortest interval you can run scheduled workflows is once every 5 minutes'; the schedule 'can be delayed during periods of high loads' and 'some queued jobs may be dropped'; schedules run only on the default branch; 'Each job in a workflow can run for up to 6 hours'; GitHub Free includes $12 of compute a month and Linux costs $0.006 a minute (about 2,000 minutes, my arithmetic). Measured: the repository is a public fork (visibility public, default branch release/v3.8.51, state on branch ccr-120121ba-vsvwlj) with 26 workflow files of the parent project.
options.cost: $0 for the daily jobs inside the included amount. A 6.5-hour engine every trading day in a private repository would be about 8,190 minutes, about $49 a month before the $12.
options.effort: 1-2 days after the move to a private repository.
options.owner_must_do: Create the private repository and add the secrets himself.
options.risks: Best-effort timing; the 6-hour cap is shorter than a trading day with pre-market; runs can stop silently when the included amount is used up; today the bot's state is in a public repository.

options.name: healthchecks.io as a second dead-man's switch (optional)
options.what_it_gives: One check per job with history and a 'down' alert by email, SMS, phone call or Pushover when a ping is late. Useful once there are more than two or three jobs to watch.
options.measured_or_documented: Documented (healthchecks.io, seen 2026-11-10): Hobbyist plan $0 with 20 checks and 100 log entries per check; period and grace 'Minimum: 60 (one minute)' each. An ntfy integration is listed on ntfy's side but I could not confirm it on healthchecks.io pages (unverified).
options.owner_must_do: Sign up himself and place the ping addresses in the environment.
options.risks: One more account; a ping address is a secret.

options.name: Keep today's design: LLM watchdog turns every 30 minutes as the only supervisor
options.what_it_gives: Nothing new. It is what ran today.
options.measured_or_documented: Measured today: 52.0% engine uptime in the first 41.9 session minutes, one stop crossed and not sold, $0.24-$0.80 of usage per wake, and a watchdog that was 285-393 s late three times.
options.cost: $0 cash; about 16 wakes a day of usage.
options.risks: The stop on a held news position is unprotected for most of each half hour unless something else keeps the VM awake.

honest_limits: 'Restart within one second' is true only for a process on a machine that is itself alive (337-449 ms in the drill). A paused or reclaimed cloud VM, a rebooted PC or a dead server cannot be brought back in a second; in Claude cloud the outside restart path is 15-30 minutes of task spacing plus a measured 37-393 s firing delay plus a 25-144 s turn.

A dead-man's switch cannot be faster than its heartbeat period plus its delay: on free ntfy about 6-9 minutes in practice (250 messages a day), on healthchecks.io at least 60 s period plus 60 s grace. It tells the owner; it restarts nothing.

The keep-awake result rests on one launch watched for 44 minutes (14:54:00 to 15:38:10 UTC). The documented cap is 2 hours per command, the feature is a research preview with no uptime promise, and the idle pause is documented only as 'a few minutes' (236-296 s is my measurement, n=3).

https://docs.ntfy.sh/publish/.replace_and_dead_man_switch: You can update or replace a scheduled message before it is delivered by publishing a new message with the same sequence ID . When you do this, the original scheduled message is deleted from the server and replaced with the new one. This is different from updating notifications after delivery, where both messages are kept in the cache. This is particularly useful for implementing a watchdog that triggers when your script stops sending heartbeat messages . This mechanism is also called a dead man's switch . For example, you could schedule a message to be delivered in 5 minutes, but continuously update it every minute to push the delivery time further into the future. If your script or system stops running, the message will eventually be delivered as an
https://docs.ntfy.sh/publish/.dead_man_example: # Dead man's switch: keeps pushing a scheduled message into the future # If this script stops, the alert will be delivered after 5 minutes while true ; do curl -H "In: 5m" -d "Warning: Server heartbeat stopped!" \ ntfy.sh/mytopic/heartbeat-check sleep
https://docs.ntfy.sh/publish/.cancel: You can cancel a scheduled message before it is delivered by sending a DELETE request to the /<topic>/<sequence_id> endpoint, just like deleting notifications . Alternatively, you can send a GET request to /<topic>/<sequence_id>/delete . This will remove the scheduled message from the server so it will never be delivered, and emit a message_delete event to any subscribers. Command line (curl) ntfy

To do this, send a DELETE request to the /<topic>/<sequence_id> endpoint. This will emit a message_delete event that is used by the clients (web app and Android app) to remove the notification entirely. Alternatively, if your client has limited HTTP support (e.g. webhooks or IoT devices), you can also delete a message by sending a GET request to /<topic>/<sequence

https://docs.ntfy.sh/subscribe/api/.scheduled: Messages that are scheduled to be delivered at a later date are not typically returned when subscribing via the API, which makes sense, because after all, the messages have technically not been delivered yet. To also return scheduled messages from the API, you can use the scheduled=1 (alias: sched=1 ) parameter (makes most sense with the poll=1 parameter): curl -s "ntfy.sh/mytopic/json?poll=1&sched=1" Replay limits
https://docs.ntfy.sh/subscribe/api/.replay_limits: Replay limits ¶ Reading cached messages (a poll=1 request, or any request with since= ) replays messages the server already stored, so unlike a live subscription its cost grows with the size of the topic's cache. Two server-side limits apply, both of which a well-behaved client should handle: The response is size-capped. A replay returns only the newest messages that fit in 10 MB per topic (counting body, title, tags and every other publisher-set field), and a capped response carries an X-Messages-Truncated: 1 header. If you see that header, older messages were dropped and you did not receive the full cache. In practice this only affects very large topics; a client polling with since= never comes close. Replayed bytes count against your daily bandwidth budget , the same one attachment downloads use (see limitations ). Exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with ntfy error code 42905 , and no mess

https://docs.ntfy.sh/config/.visitor: A visitor is identified by its IP address (or the X-Forwarded-For header if behind-proxy is set). All config o
https://docs.ntfy.sh/config/.http_429: When a rate limit is hit, the server responds with HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). If the server knows when the request would be allowed again, the response carries a Retry-After header with the number of seconds to wait: until the visitor's bucket has refilled enough (e.g. for the request, e-mail or topic creation limits), or until the visitor's day is over for a daily limit (e.g. messages, e-mails, phone calls or attachment bandwidth).
